paragraphs: Distributional temporal difference learning estimates the distribution of future discounted returns for a fixed policy. That is a richer target than the usual value function, which captures only the expected return. This paper asks how much streaming data is needed to learn that richer target when predictions use linear function approximation.

Earlier statistical analyses mainly addressed tabular settings. The authors derive sharp finite-sample rates for the linear approximation setting, making the amount of available data an explicit part of the guarantee. Their central finding is that the sample complexity matches that of conventional linear temporal difference learning.

The proof combines a detailed analysis of the linear-categorical Bellman equation with exponential stability arguments for products of random matrices. The significance is statistical: within the analyzed setting, estimating a full return distribution does not require a worse sample-complexity rate than estimating its mean. This provides a theoretical reason to view richer return predictions as compatible with sample-efficient learning, rather than automatically assuming that a richer prediction target demands more observations.
neurips-2025-a-finite-sample-analysis-of.tldr: The paper proves that linear distributional TD learning matches the sample-complexity rates of learning expected returns in its analyzed setting.

paragraphs: Spiking neural networks communicate through discrete activity events. Their event-driven operation makes reducing neuronal activity a direct route to reducing computation, particularly for deployment on neuromorphic hardware. This paper targets that activity itself, extending the pursuit of efficiency beyond reducing the number of model parameters.

The authors first analyze why existing activity regularization methods struggle to train sparse spiking networks. They then introduce a modified neuron model, AT-LIF, together with a threshold adaptation technique. The combination is designed to stabilize training while suppressing spike activity, addressing the tension between keeping neurons quiet and preserving a useful learning process.

Experiments across multiple datasets show substantial reductions in average firing rates and synaptic operations while sacrificing little accuracy. The approach also complements pruning of network weights. On ImageNet, the authors report training a model with an average firing rate of 0.06 and 2.22 million parameters. Together, these findings support combining sparse activity with sparse connectivity to build more computationally efficient spiking models.
neurips-2025-activity-pruning-for-effici.tldr: An adaptive neuron design reduces spiking activity and computation with little accuracy loss while complementing weight pruning.

paragraphs: Assembling a three-dimensional object from separate parts requires both an overall understanding of the object and precise decisions about where each component belongs. CFPA addresses these two demands through a coarse-to-fine process that combines high-level semantic organization with detailed geometric pose refinement.

The first stage constructs semantic super-parts using an optimal transport formulation. These larger groupings capture object structure, and a dual-range feature propagation mechanism passes that information back to individual components. The second stage combines information across stages with geometry specific to each part instance, refining positions and orientations for a more spatially coherent assembly.

The training objective also accounts for symmetry within a part and geometric similarity between parts. This supports different valid arrangements while maintaining structural consistency. Experiments on PartNet report state-of-the-art assembly accuracy, consistency, and diversity across multiple categories. The contribution is therefore a coordinated treatment of global structure, local precision, and valid variation: all three influence which assemblies the model learns to produce.
neurips-2025-coarse-to-fine-3d-part-asse.tldr: CFPA combines semantic grouping, geometric refinement, and symmetry-aware training to assemble accurate and diverse 3D objects.

paragraphs: A single model learning several tasks can encounter conflicting optimization directions and uneven progress across tasks. Many approaches respond by changing the weights assigned to task losses or gradients. COST instead explores whether moving to a different parameter configuration with an equivalent loss can make subsequent optimization less conflicted.

When a conflict arises, the method searches for such an alternative point on the loss landscape. It implements this symmetry-based movement using a low-rank adapter, or LoRA, and objectives designed to converge while preserving loss. The purpose is to change the optimization situation without first requiring an improvement in the loss value.

COST also reuses historical optimization trajectories to retain the benefits of advanced optimizers over continued training. Experiments on multiple mainstream datasets demonstrate improvements across a broad range of existing multi-task methods, including superior results when combined with state-of-the-art approaches. Its plug-and-play design matters because the proposed movement can augment established training methods, providing another way to address conflict within a shared model.
neurips-2025-continual-optimization-with.tldr: COST reduces multi-task optimization conflict by moving between loss-equivalent parameter configurations and reusing optimization history.

paragraphs: Estimating a treatment's causal effect becomes difficult when an unobserved factor influences both treatment and outcome. This paper studies an approach that uses two separate sets of proxy measurements associated with treatment and outcomes. Under appropriate assumptions, these measurements support estimation through a function called the causal bridge.

The authors develop a new theoretical perspective on that bridge and specify assumptions under which treatment-effect estimation is feasible. They also derive a bound on average treatment-effect error when the bridge assumptions are violated. This connects the method's causal interpretation to explicit conditions and examines what happens when those conditions do not hold.

Building on the theory, the method couples the causal bridge with an autoencoder. This lets information from proxies, treatments, and outcomes contribute jointly to estimation, improving the quality of the learned bridge. Experiments using synthetic and real-world data demonstrate effectiveness relative to state-of-the-art methods for causal inference with proxies. The approach links a conditional causal identification strategy with a representation-learning architecture that shares information across observed quantities.
neurips-2025-coupling-generative-modelin.tldr: Coupling a causal bridge with an autoencoder improves treatment-effect estimation from proxies under stated causal assumptions.

paragraphs: Creative image editing asks a system to introduce expressive, original transformations while keeping an image coherent and aligned with artistic intent. The paper frames this as a broader problem than executing a direct editing instruction: deciding how an image should evolve is itself part of the work.

CREA organizes that work around a collaborating team of specialized AI agents. Their roles cover developing concepts, generating images, critiquing results, and enhancing them. These activities form an autonomous, iterative process inspired by human creative work, allowing the framework to revisit and develop an image through collaboration.

The authors evaluate CREA both qualitatively and quantitatively, reporting significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods in diversity, semantic alignment, and creative transformation. These dimensions matter together because originality alone does not establish that an edit remains meaningful or coherent. The reported findings support organizing image creation around an ongoing cycle of proposals and critique. The authors also position the paper, to their knowledge, as the first introduction of creative editing as a task.
neurips-2025-crea-a-collaborative-multi-.tldr: CREA uses collaborating agents to conceive, generate, critique, and refine images, improving evaluated creative editing outcomes.

paragraphs: This paper examines an expressivity constraint associated with highly parallel Transformer computation. Under logarithmic precision, the abstract places standard Transformers within the complexity class TC⁰. It points to state-tracking problems, including code evaluation and entity tracking, as important tasks generally considered outside that class.

Recent state-space approaches using the Delta Rule can exceed this expressivity restriction, but the authors identify fixed-size state spaces as a limitation that affects performance on many tasks. DeltaFormer is motivated by bringing the strengths of these perspectives together. It revisits the Transformer as a state-space model expressed through kernel functions and uses that interpretation to develop an improved architecture.

The authors report theoretical and practical evidence that DeltaFormer exceeds the stated TC⁰ restriction of standard Transformers. They also verify that it is no weaker than the standard Transformer on the language-modeling tasks considered. The result connects architectural expressivity with practical modeling performance: expanding the kinds of computation an architecture can represent need not come at the expense of the reported language-modeling capability.
neurips-2025-deltaformer-unlock-the-stat.tldr: DeltaFormer uses a kernel-based state-space perspective to exceed a stated Transformer expressivity bound while retaining tested language-modeling performance.

paragraphs: Vector-quantized variational autoencoders represent continuous inputs through learned discrete codes. This paper finds that their apparently high-dimensional embeddings often occupy a much smaller subspace, typically just four to ten dimensions. The authors call this pattern dimensional collapse and analyze its relationship to model performance and learning dynamics.

A central observation is that directly forcing representations to use more dimensions can degrade performance. The models appear to favor a low-dimensional regime, so increasing effective dimensionality through rank regularization is not automatically beneficial. This motivates a remedy that accommodates the observed learning behavior while expanding the capacity available to the overall representation.

Divide-and-Conquer VQ partitions the latent space into several low-dimensional subspaces and quantizes each independently. Each component can operate in the regime the model tends to prefer, while their combination provides greater overall capacity. Results across image datasets show improved reconstruction quality and support the method as a way to overcome the observed bottleneck. The design turns the collapse analysis into a concrete change in how quantization is organized.
neurips-2025-dimensional-collapse-in-vqv.tldr: DCVQ improves reconstruction by combining independently quantized low-dimensional subspaces to address dimensional collapse in VQVAEs.

paragraphs: High-resolution volumetric 3D generation places heavy demands on memory and computation. Direct3D-S2 addresses this through sparse volumes and an attention mechanism designed specifically for their spatial organization. The goal is to make detailed volumetric generation practical while improving the quality of generated shapes.

Its Spatial Sparse Attention mechanism makes diffusion Transformer computation more efficient on large sets of sparse-volume tokens. The authors report forward-pass and backward-pass speedups of 3.9 times and 9.6 times, respectively. A complementary variational autoencoder preserves the same sparse volumetric format at the input, latent, and output stages, improving training efficiency and stability compared with designs that mix representations.

Experiments on public datasets report better generation quality and efficiency than state-of-the-art methods. The framework also trains at 1024³ resolution on eight GPUs. The abstract contrasts this with typical volumetric training requirements of at least 32 GPUs at 256³ resolution. Together, the attention mechanism and unified representation show how changes throughout the pipeline can substantially expand the resolution accessible with a smaller hardware allocation.
neurips-2025-direct3d-s2-gigascale-3d-ge.tldr: Direct3D-S2 combines spatial sparse attention with a unified sparse-volume autoencoder to enable efficient, high-resolution 3D generation.

paragraphs: Reaching a local minimum does not establish that a model has found the lowest loss or the best generalization available in parameter space. This paper proposes an adaptor called E that encourages gradient-based optimizers to keep exploring after reaching such a point, using valleys where losses remain low and nearly equal.

The adapted optimizer tends to move along these valleys in search of potentially better local minima. The intended benefit is a greater likelihood of reaching a lower and flatter minimum, a property often associated with better generalization. The authors also provide convergence proofs for adapted optimizers in both convex and non-convex settings.

The empirical evaluation focuses on large-minibatch training, described as a difficult optimization setting. Applying the adaptor to Lamb produces ALTO, which improves test accuracy by an average of 2.5% over the current state-of-the-art optimizer across the evaluated large-batch tasks. These results support continued exploration as a useful optimizer design principle, while the proposed mechanism seeks better minima without claiming to guarantee the best possible one.
neurips-2025-exploring-landscapes-for-be.tldr: The E adaptor encourages optimizers to explore low-loss valleys, with its Lamb variant improving accuracy in evaluated large-batch training tasks.

paragraphs: Selective state-space models form the central architectural component of Mamba and offer an alternative to Transformers for sequence modeling. This paper develops a theoretical account of their generalization behavior, connecting analysis of this architecture to recent advances in understanding Transformer models.

The main result is a generalization bound based on covering numbers. The authors use that bound to study how a property of the continuous-time state matrix, its spectral abscissa, affects training stability and generalization across sequence lengths. This makes the internal state dynamics central to the analysis of whether behavior learned during training carries over to other sequence lengths.

The theoretical findings are examined empirically on a synthetic majority task, IMDb sentiment classification, and ListOps. These experiments demonstrate how the insights correspond to practical model behavior across the tested settings. The contribution therefore combines a mathematical bound with an architectural interpretation and empirical checks. It provides a way to reason about selective state-space models through their dynamics, while drawing on tools developed for attention-based architectures.
neurips-2025-generalization-error-analys.tldr: A new generalization bound connects selective state-space model dynamics to training stability and generalization across sequence lengths.

paragraphs: Graph classification commonly assumes that the relevant categories are already known. This paper introduces Graph-Level Novel Category Discovery, which asks models to identify previously unseen graph categories without supervision from those new classes. The authors curate four graph datasets to study this setting.

Adapting existing image-based category-discovery methods reveals substantial performance degradation. The analysis identifies two problems: self-supervised learning makes insufficient use of graph structure, and ranking-based pseudo-labeling also neglects that structure. Both weaknesses concern how graphs are compared and grouped, motivating a method that places structural information inside those operations.

The proposed ProtoFGW-NCD framework combines a graph self-supervised learning component with structure-aware pseudo-labeling. Both use a differentiable Fused Gromov-Wasserstein distance and learnable prototype graphs. The prototypes capture representative patterns and enable efficient parallel comparisons using that distance. Experiments on all four benchmarks demonstrate the framework's effectiveness. The paper contributes both a new evaluation task and an approach that adapts category discovery to the structural information that distinguishes graphs from images.
neurips-2025-glncd-graph-level-novel-cat.tldr: ProtoFGW-NCD uses graph prototypes and structure-aware comparisons to discover unseen graph categories without labels for those classes.

paragraphs: Unsigned distance fields naturally represent open surfaces, but converting them into explicit triangle meshes is challenging. At high resolutions, noise in neural distance fields can obscure fine details. Methods that make decisions within individual voxels can leave holes or omit surfaces when local evidence is ambiguous.

The proposed iterative neural network repeatedly revisits surface extraction while incorporating neighboring information. Each pass uses previously recovered surface elements together with distance values and gradients. As iterations proceed, information propagates from increasingly distant neighbors, allowing the network to improve decisions that were difficult to make from a voxel's own evidence.

Experiments on diverse 3D models show substantially more accurate and complete meshes than existing approaches, particularly for complex geometry. The method also supports higher-resolution extraction in cases where traditional techniques fail. Its central contribution is to make surface recovery a process of progressive correction: newly detected geometry becomes useful evidence for later extraction, helping stabilize challenging regions and recover details that isolated, single-pass decisions can miss.
neurips-2025-high-resolution-udf-meshing.tldr: An iterative network uses neighboring surface evidence to extract more complete and accurate high-resolution meshes from unsigned distance fields.

paragraphs: Black-box attacks on vision-language models must work with accessible predictions while accounting for both text and images. The paper identifies shortcomings in existing approaches: complicated alternating searches consume many queries, while simply reducing similarity between matching image-text pairs can also reduce similarity to mismatched pairs and weaken the attack.

HQA-VLAttack separates the process into text and image stages. The text stage uses counter-fitting word vectors to construct substitute-word sets that preserve semantic consistency. The image stage begins with a layer-importance-guided initialization, then uses a contrastive objective to shape the perturbation.

That objective pushes matching image-text pairs apart while pulling mismatched pairs closer together. The two directions matter because the attack aims to make the model retrieve incorrect matches, not merely weaken correct ones. Experiments on three benchmark datasets report significantly higher attack success rates than strong baselines. The findings support coordinating text substitutions with image perturbations that explicitly account for both positive and negative pair relationships in the evaluated retrieval setting.
neurips-2025-hqa-vlattack-towards-high-q.tldr: HQA-VLAttack combines semantic word substitutions with contrastive image perturbations to improve black-box vision-language attack success.

paragraphs: This paper studies whether better training-data selection can improve neural reconstruction for accelerated MRI. Much work in this area concentrates on network architecture while using fixed, relatively homogeneous datasets. The authors shift attention to data curation and evaluate reconstruction across a wider range of imaging conditions.

They assemble raw k-space data from 18 public sources, totaling 1.1 million images. Their evaluation contains 48 test sets covering differences in anatomy, contrast, coil count, and other factors. This setup allows the study to examine filtering strategies across varied conditions rather than drawing conclusions from a single homogeneous test set.

Filtering yields consistent but modest performance improvements for current state-of-the-art reconstruction networks. The gains persist across different training-set sizes and acceleration levels, and filtering is particularly helpful when the original training collection contains a small proportion of in-distribution data. The finding gives data composition a concrete role in reconstruction quality: selecting more suitable examples can improve results even when the underlying network is already strong.
neurips-2025-improving-deep-learning-for.tldr: Filtering a diverse MRI training collection produces consistent, modest reconstruction gains, especially when initially relevant data are scarce.

paragraphs: This paper introduces π-Quant, an optimizer-state compression algorithm intended to reduce the memory needed for training. Its starting point is a mathematical representation result: using a complex rotation scheme with properties of irrational numbers, a pair of parameters can be represented through a single rotation angle.

The algorithm maps parameters into complex space and quantizes their associated rotation angles. This changes the representation on which compression operates, making the geometry of paired values central to the method. To integrate the scheme efficiently into optimization, the authors develop geometric equations that calculate the required angles precisely with linear complexity.

Across a wide range of evaluated tasks, the authors report reducing parameter bit width to 3.32 bits and lowering GPU memory usage by 41.8% while maintaining full accuracy. These are empirical results for the evaluated settings. The contribution joins a mathematical encoding idea with an efficient angle-computation procedure, showing how a compact representation can translate into substantial training-memory savings without an observed accuracy reduction in those experiments.
neurips-2025-irrational-complex-rotation.tldr: π-Quant compresses optimizer states through complex rotation angles, reporting 41.8% lower GPU memory usage while preserving accuracy in its experiments.

paragraphs: Genesys investigates whether language models can organize the discovery of new language-model architectures. Its multi-agent workflow covers proposal development and literature search, implementation, pretraining, and downstream evaluation. Designs are also adversarially reviewed, making criticism part of the discovery process before increasingly expensive verification.

The system uses a Ladder of Scales, evaluating selected candidates at progressively larger sizes between 14 million and 350 million parameters while reducing the number trained at each stage. A genetic programming backbone structures design generation. The authors report an approximately 86-percentage-point improvement in successful design generation over commonly used direct-prompt workflows, addressing a key bottleneck in the process.

Experiments include 1,162 new designs, of which 1,062 are fully verified. The best are competitive with established architectures and outperform examples including GPT2 and Mamba2 on six of nine common benchmarks. System-level ablations and formal results accompany the empirical findings. The contribution concerns both the discovered architectures and how structured generation, review, and staged investment can support autonomous architecture research.
neurips-2025-language-modeling-by-langua.tldr: Genesys combines multi-agent research, genetic programming, and staged training to discover language-model architectures competitive with established designs.

paragraphs: Preference alignment seeks to make language-model responses reflect human preferences. Synthetic preference data can make this training more scalable and economical, but its distribution may differ from the human-preferred distribution. This paper addresses the resulting mismatch through a training objective that explicitly accounts for relevance to the target distribution.

The method first uses well-learned classifiers to assign each training example a calibration value. That value expresses how closely the example aligns with the intended human-preferred distribution. The values then enter a robust optimization objective that minimizes worst-case loss over regions of the data space most relevant to those preferences.

This connects two decisions that can otherwise be treated separately: assessing which examples represent the desired preferences and deciding where training should guard against poor performance. The authors state that the framework mitigates distributional mismatch and improves responses' alignment with intended values. Its central contribution is a distribution-aware approach to preference optimization, with classifier-based calibration guiding the regions emphasized by the robust objective.
neurips-2025-leveraging-robust-optimizat.tldr: Classifier-calibrated robust optimization focuses preference training on the human-preferred distribution to mitigate synthetic-data mismatch.

paragraphs: Placing an object into an image or 3D scene requires its lighting and shadows to fit the surrounding environment. Maintaining that fit across viewpoints adds another challenge. MV-CoLight addresses illumination-consistent compositing in both 2D and 3D, with applications motivated by augmented reality and embodied intelligence.

The proposed two-stage framework uses a feed-forward architecture that models lighting and shadows directly. The authors present this as a way to avoid iterative biases associated with diffusion-based methods. A Hilbert curve-based mapping aligns image inputs with 3D Gaussian scene representations, connecting the image-level information to the representation used for a three-dimensional scene.

The paper also introduces a large-scale 3D compositing dataset for training and evaluation. Experiments report state-of-the-art harmonization on standard benchmarks and the new dataset, while results on casually captured real scenes demonstrate robustness and broad generalization. The contribution combines an efficient compositing architecture with a bridge between 2D inputs and 3D representations, supporting consistent appearance across the settings examined.
neurips-2025-mv-colight-efficient-object.tldr: MV-CoLight directly models lighting and shadows to composite objects consistently into images and 3D Gaussian scenes.

paragraphs: Multi-objective optimization involves finding solutions that balance competing goals. Pareto Set Learning uses a neural network to model the set of Pareto-optimal solutions. Applying this idea to black-box objectives becomes difficult when problems are high-dimensional, involve strong dependencies between dimensions, or have other complex properties.

Neural-ES brings evolution strategies into Pareto Set Learning to address those difficulties. The authors identify inefficient handling of dependencies between dimensions as a weakness of traditional evolution strategies in this setting. Their method represents those dependencies within a neural network and trains it using a new gradient-estimation procedure.

Evaluation uses a benchmark suite designed specifically for black-box Pareto Set Learning. Comparisons with other methods demonstrate the efficiency of Neural-ES and its ability to learn Pareto sets for challenging problems. The approach matters because the learning target is a collection of trade-off solutions, making dependencies across the search space relevant to the whole set. Its contribution combines a neural representation of those dependencies with an optimization strategy suited to black-box objectives.
neurips-2025-neural-evolution-strategy-f.tldr: Neural-ES models dependencies between dimensions to improve evolution-strategy learning of Pareto sets for difficult black-box objectives.

paragraphs: SHAP explanations are widely used, but they can overlook the causal relationships underlying a problem. do-SHAP addresses this by using intervention-based queries. Its practical difficulty is a reliance on estimands, which complicates application when the causal graph and the required queries become complex.

This paper proposes using estimand-agnostic causal inference to estimate any identifiable query from a single model. That shared model makes do-SHAP feasible on complex graphs. Identifiability remains an explicit condition: the proposal supports queries whose causal effects can be identified, rather than claiming that a single model resolves every causal question.

The authors also introduce an algorithm that substantially accelerates computation at negligible cost and a method for explaining inaccessible data-generating processes. They demonstrate estimation and computational performance and validate the approach on two real-world datasets. The contribution addresses several practical obstacles together, linking a reusable causal inference model with faster explanation computation. The reported results highlight the potential for more reliable explanations that incorporate causal structure.
neurips-2025-practical-do-shapley-explan.tldr: A shared causal inference model and faster computation make intervention-based do-SHAP explanations more practical for complex graphs.

paragraphs: Some data-poisoning methods are intended to support ownership verification or protect private data from unauthorized use. Their resemblance to harmful poisoning can nevertheless create confusion and conflict. This paper proposes watermarking generated poisoned datasets so that ownership can be claimed and users can identify potential poisoning.

The authors develop two approaches: adding a watermark after poisoning and incorporating watermarking during the poisoning process. Their analysis gives watermark-length conditions under which detectability and poisoning utility are both guaranteed. For post-poisoning watermarking, the stated length scales as Θ(√d/ε_w); for concurrent watermarking, the stated range extends from Θ(1/ε_w²) to O(√d/ε_p).

These are conditional guarantees tied to the specified scaling requirements. They establish that making the watermark detectable can coexist with preserving the poisoning's intended effect. Experiments across several attacks, models, and datasets validate the theoretical findings. The contribution is an attribution mechanism for poisoned data, with theory and experiments addressing whether attribution remains possible without removing the utility that motivated the data modification.
neurips-2025-provable-watermarking-for-d.tldr: Two watermarking schemes provide conditional guarantees that poisoned datasets remain attributable while preserving poisoning utility.

paragraphs: Remote-sensing vision-language models depend on image-text data that capture meaningful relationships between visual content and descriptions. Such paired data are harder to obtain at scale than for natural images. This paper addresses quality assessment for synthetically generated remote-sensing data, an area the authors identify as lacking a systematic automated framework.

The proposed scoring model learns from large-scale remote-sensing vision-language preference data. It ranks generated training examples by quality. In the reported experiments, fine-tuning CLIP or more advanced models such as Qwen2-VL on the highest-ranked 30% yields better accuracy than using the full dataset or selecting examples through CLIP scores.

The scoring model also supports reinforcement-learning training and best-of-N selection at test time, with significant improvements reported for remote-sensing tasks. Its role therefore extends beyond filtering a fixed training collection to guiding learning and choosing outputs. The results show that learned quality assessment can make a smaller selected dataset more effective in the evaluated settings while providing a reusable signal for other stages of model improvement.
neurips-2025-quality-driven-curation-of-.tldr: A learned quality scorer improves remote-sensing vision-language models through data selection, reinforcement learning, and test-time candidate selection.

paragraphs: Adversarial inputs can shift CLIP embeddings enough to affect systems that depend on them, including image generators and large vision-language models. Work on robust CLIP models has focused on image encoders. This paper addresses the text side with LEAF, an adversarial fine-tuning method designed to scale to large CLIP models.

LEAF significantly improves zero-shot adversarial accuracy for text while maintaining the visual performance supplied by robust image encoders. This matters for a model whose image and text representations are used together: improving the image component alone leaves the text component as another source of sensitivity.

The authors examine several downstream effects. Combined with text-to-image diffusion models, robust text encoders improve generation quality under adversarial noise. LEAF also improves multimodal retrieval recall under such noise compared with standard CLIP. Finally, direct optimization reconstructs input text more effectively from the robust embeddings. These findings show benefits across several evaluated uses of the text representation, connecting encoder robustness to the behavior of systems built around CLIP.
neurips-2025-robustness-in-both-domains-.tldr: LEAF strengthens CLIP's text encoder against adversarial inputs while retaining robust vision performance and improving evaluated downstream tasks.

paragraphs: Styl3R generates a stylized 3D scene from sparse scene images without supplied poses and an arbitrary style image. The paper reports doing so in less than a second through feed-forward reconstruction. This addresses the substantial test-time optimization and dense posed imagery often required by existing 3D stylization methods.

Its branched architecture separates modeling scene structure from shading its appearance. The separation is designed to keep artistic changes from distorting the underlying geometry, addressing the tension between reconstructing a scene and transforming its visual style. An adapted identity loss supports pretraining through novel-view synthesis and helps retain reconstruction capability during stylization fine-tuning.

Evaluations on both in-domain and out-of-domain datasets report high-quality stylized 3D outputs with a stronger combination of scene appearance and reference style. The method also outperforms existing approaches in multi-view consistency and efficiency. Together, these findings support a direct reconstruction-and-stylization pipeline in which structure and appearance have distinct roles, allowing rapid artistic transformation while maintaining coherent views of the reconstructed scene.
neurips-2025-styl3r-instant-3d-stylized-.tldr: Styl3R reconstructs stylized 3D scenes in under a second by separating scene structure from appearance in a feed-forward model.
